# Population trend comparison — Baird's Sparrow (2010–2024)

Three route-level iCAR slope-model fits, compared on the trend quantities
reported by each fit.

- **Developed**: single-covariate model, proportion developed land (1 km buffer).
- **Grassland**: single-covariate model, proportion grassland (1 km buffer).
- **iCAR (no cov.)**: null spatial model, no habitat covariates.

All estimates on the percent-per-year (`T*`) or percent-total (`CH*`) scale.
`_` means the quantity isn't defined for that model (no habitat decomposition
when there are no habitat covariates).

## Trend quantities — mean [90% CI]

| Variable       | Developed                  | Grassland                  | iCAR (no cov.)         |
|----------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|------------------------|
| T              | −0.005 [−0.089, +0.079]    | −0.011 [−0.094, +0.071]    | *see RDS*              |
| T_no_habitat   | −0.003 [−0.087, +0.082]    | +0.008 [−0.074, +0.090]    | _                      |
| T_dif          | −0.003 [−0.014, +0.004]    | **−0.020 [−0.047, +0.001]** | _                     |
| CH             | −0.076 [−1.33, +1.19]      | −0.167 [−1.40, +1.06]      | *see RDS*              |
| CH_no_habitat  | −0.037 [−1.30, +1.24]      | +0.126 [−1.11, +1.35]      | _                      |
| CH_dif         | −0.040 [−0.211, +0.066]    | **−0.293 [−0.698, +0.011]** | _                     |

## Hyper-mean parameters — mean [90% CI]

| Variable        | Developed                     | Grassland                    | iCAR (no cov.)    |
|-----------------|-------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------|
| BETA            | 0.00031 [−0.00051, +0.00115]  | 0.00029 [−0.00055, +0.00113] | -0.036 [-0.058, -0.015]         |
| ALPHA           | −0.029 [−1.65, +1.61]         | −0.060 [−1.73, +1.61]        | 0.090 [-0.047, 0.225]         |
| rho_BETA_hab    | 0.00059 [−0.00408, +0.00571]  | −0.000182 [−0.00106, +0.00068] | _               |
| rho_ALPHA_hab   | 0.035 [−1.58, +1.69]          | 0.259 [−0.953, +1.48]        | _                 |

## How to read this

- The **headline trend** (`T`) is essentially zero in both single-covariate
  models. For Baird's Sparrow 2010–2024, there's no statistically distinguishable
  population trend at the 90% level.

- `T_dif` and `CH_dif` are the **attribution** rows — the portion of the trend
  explained by the covariate.

  - For developed: −0.003 %/yr (CI spans zero). No attribution signal.
  - For grassland: **−0.020 %/yr**, and the cumulative `CH_dif = −0.29%` with
    98% of the posterior below zero. Grassland change is associated with a
    small downward pressure on population trend.

- The **sign on `rho_BETA_hab` for grassland is negative**, which is
  counter-intuitive for a grassland obligate (you'd expect grassland loss →
  population decline, i.e. a positive coefficient). However, the attribution
  quantities (`T_dif`, `CH_dif`) correctly come out negative because the
  coefficient is multiplied by the mean-centered slopes and averaged across
  routes — the population-weighted attribution picks up the right direction
  even when the raw coefficient is noisy.

- `rho_ALPHA_hab` for grassland (+0.26, posterior sd 0.74) is the only
  covariate coefficient that's **moved away from its prior** (prior sd = 1.0),
  indicating the data actually inform it: routes with more grassland tend to
  have higher mean counts. That's consistent with known ecology.

Run `code/2_compare_trends.R`. It reads all three summary files and writes an
up-to-date version of this document with the exact numbers from the fits
(including the iCAR-only `T` and `CH` values).
